title: Its Time to Discard the Sandwich Technique for Giving Feedback
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues against the classic 'praise-criticism-praise' sandwich method of delivering feedback, noting that recipients quickly learn to see the bookend compliments as insincere padding around the real criticism. Rather than abandoning the instinct to open with something positive, the author reframes the fix: make the opening positive statement as detailed and specific as the criticism that follows, so it reads as genuine rather than a buffer. Backed by research on people's tendency to overweight negative feedback, the piece argues that a substantive positive opener creates balance rather than manipulation. It closes with a call to replace the 'crap sandwich' with feedback that feels fair rather than formulaic.
points: The Sandwich Technique often backfires because recipients learn to discount the bookend praise as insincere filler.
The fix isn't dropping the positive opener, but making it as specific and detailed as the criticism that follows.
Research on negativity bias supports leading with a substantive positive statement to create balance, not manipulation.
Feedback that feels sincere and thorough, rather than formulaic, produces less defensiveness and more openness.
quotes: In many organizations, the technique is known as a Crap Sandwich because everyone knows that the center of the sandwich tastes like rubbish.
After a few experiences with this technique, those on the receiving end often feel manipulated by it.
The key is to make this positive statement as detailed and vivid as the criticism will likely be.
The more specific, thorough, and elaborate the positive statement, the more likely it is to be seen as sincere and genuine.
Going straight to the criticism or attempting to offset it with an artificial affirmation creates heavy resistance and encourages people to reject what they are hearing.
Kill the sandwich technique and replace it with feedback that operates in balance.
